Captain Harry Brook says leaning on a mentor of Kevin Pietersen's calibre will only help the continued upward trajectory of England's white-ball sides. Pietersen, regarded as one of the greatest batters of the 21st century, has been brought into the England white-ball set-up in a mentoring role by head coach Brendon McCullum in the build-up to next year's 50-over World Cup. Brook shed light on the impact Pietersen was already having on the squad, both on and off the field, with the team's approach to playing spin already addressed in a masterclass from the former England captain. messages.text: Trott replaces Flintoff as England Lions head coach

metadata.summary: Jonathan Trott will coach the England Lions this winter, filling the role vacated by Andrew Flintoff.
metadata.content: England Lions: Jonathan Trott replaces Andrew Flintoff as head coach of development squad for winter tours | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England Lions: Jonathan Trott replaces Andrew Flintoff as head coach of development squad for winter tours Jonathan Trott has committed to coaching the England Lions this winter on tours of West Indies, South Africa and Sri Lanka; Trott fills the void left by Andrew Flintoff standing down from the role in August; Trott won the Ashes three times during 52 Test appearances for England Monday 21 September 2026 14:31, UK Image: Jonathan Trott will take charge of the England Lions this winter Jonathan Trott will coach the England Lions this winter, filling the role vacated by Andrew Flintoff. Flintoff stood down from the position with immediate effect in August, with Trott stepping in to lead the side's recent T20 series win over the touring Sri Lanka side. Now the three-time Ashes winner, who previously enjoyed success as head coach of Afghanistan, has agreed to stay in post for next six months. metadata.summary: Luke Littler has withdrawn from two Players Championship events in the Netherlands less than 24 hours after his bid for a PDC majors title clean sweep was dashed.
metadata.content: Luke Littler withdraws from Players Championship events after hopes of PDC title sweep dashed | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Luke Littler withdraws from Players Championship events after hopes of PDC title sweep dashed Luke Littler has withdrawn from two Players Championship events in the Netherlands after his hopes of completing a clean sweep of PDC major titles this season ended in Amsterdam; the world No 1 had already threatened to boycott Dutch events after crowd abuse Monday 21 September 2026 11:49, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jonny Clayton ended Luke Littler's clean sweep at the World Series of Darts Finals. Credit: @OfficialPDC. Luke Littler has withdrawn from two Players Championship events in the Netherlands less than 24 hours after his bid for a PDC majors title clean sweep was dashed. World No 1 Littler was dumped out of the World Series of Darts Finals at the quarter-final stage by a 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton on Sunday, ending his run of winning the first six premier events of the season. The 19-year-old had been scheduled to feature at Players Championship 29 and 30 in Den Bosch, Netherlands, on Tuesday and Wednesday but has pulled out of both events, a decision which effectively ends his chances of qualifying for November's finals in Minehead.
